 MKS (MKSI) Beat Q3 Guidance, Is The Stock Still Cheap?
 Sasha Jovanovic Sat, November 7, 2026 at 11:06 PM PST 3 min read MKSI +8.74% 
 Trade MKS on Coinbase Trading disclosure Trading disclosure

 Learn more MKS (MKSI) is back in focus after a packed early November update that combined third quarter results, fresh fourth quarter guidance, a new US$500 million buyback and a quarterly dividend affirmation. 
 All of this lands at a share price of US$192.27 after an 8.74% 1 day share price gain, even though the 30 day share price return is down 27.31% and the 90 day share price return is down 34.23%. The 3 year total shareholder return of 176.73% points to strong longer term momentum that recent volatility has softened rather than reversed. 
 Spot emerging peers riding the same semiconductor and AI surge as MKS by scanning our hand picked 53 AI infrastructure stocks . 
 MKS now trades at a steep discount to both a US$350.57 analyst target and its own intrinsic estimate, even after the latest jump. Is that a mispricing, or a clear warning that the market is right to be cautious? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 53% Undervalued 
 MKS is framed by the most followed thesis as significantly undervalued, with a fair value of $410.86 against the latest close at $192.27. That gap rests on a very specific growth and margin story playing out. 
 The company's push toward a larger base of recurring chemistry and service revenue, with high chemistry gross margins and service income supported by fabs running near full utilization, increases the proportion of annuity like sales and can support more resilient net margins and earnings across cycles. 
 See why 19 investors see MKS as 53% undervalued . 
 Result: Fair Value of $410.86 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, the bullish MKS story can crack if AI related semiconductor spending cools or if new Malaysia and Guangzhou capacity keeps margins under pressure for longer.
